title: Microsoft Teams: private chat for organisers and presenters in webinars, structured meetings and town halls
summary: Hold: the statement that Microsoft Learn does not explain where event group chat is stored overlooks Microsoft's published storage rules for Teams group chats. The rollout facts and the documented meeting and attendee-chat controls are supported; the backroom policy path remains undocumented.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The event chat storage rule excludes event group chat from organiser-mailbox storage for up to 30 days.
claims.quote: Meeting chat messages in events optimized for large audiences, excluding the event group chat, are stored only in an organizer's mailbox for up to 30 days.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not say where event group chat messages are stored instead.
claims.quote: All Microsoft Teams 1:1 or group chats are journaled through to the respective users' mailboxes.
claims.fix: Replace the repeated storage-absence wording with: "The Manage chat for Teams events article excludes event group chat from its attendee-chat storage rule. Microsoft's general Teams group-chat documentation places compliance copies in participants' Exchange Online mailboxes." Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/edisc-search-teams. Replace the storage open question with "Can our compliance staff retrieve a test event group chat from its participants' mailboxes?" Keep the proposed tenant test.

claims.claim: Teams chat data is kept in a hidden folder in each included user's mailbox.
claims.quote: Data from Teams chats is stored in a hidden folder in the mailbox of each user included in the chat, and a similar hidden folder in a group mailbox is used for Teams channel messages.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Compliance administrators can search the hidden Teams message data with eDiscovery tools.
claims.quote: These hidden folders aren't designed to be directly accessible to users or administrators, but instead, store data that compliance administrators can search with eDiscovery tools.

claims.claim: External presenter support for event group chat is covered by a separate roadmap item.
claims.quote: "id": 573706; "title": "Microsoft Teams: External presenter support for event group chat"; "description": "Event group chat, the private chat for organizers, co-organizers, and presenters in an event or structured meeting, will support external presenters."
claims.fix: Add Microsoft 365 Roadmap 573706 to sources at https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/roadmap?id=573706; the linked wiki briefing is not evidence for this record fact.

claims.claim: The described feature is person-to-person chat rather than an autonomous action mechanism.
claims.quote: This separate chat enhances collaboration by allowing key participants to communicate privately before, during, and after the event, without involving attendees.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; controls[0].api; Why it matters; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no town hall backroom chat policy path or automation operation.
claims.quote: Searched: backroom chat Teams admin center; event group chat Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy Graph. Read plan-events, manage-event-chat, both Teams policy references, onlineMeeting beta, virtualEventTownhall beta and virtualEventSettings beta; no documented backroom control.

claims.claim: Plan for Teams events lists no admin control for event group chat, unlike MC1188222.
claims.quote: Event group chat (organizers, co-organizers, and presenters) | No control. | Can chat with presenters and co-organizers. Attendees don't use this chat during events.

claims.claim: Meeting chat is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting engagement > Meeting chat.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Meeting policies. Select the policy you want to edit. Go to the Meeting engagement section. Set Meeting chat to your chosen value

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -MeetingChatEnabledType Disabled is the documented call to turn meeting chat off.
claims.quote: To turn off meeting chat for users with this assigned policy, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -MeetingChatEnabledType Disabled

claims.claim: Meeting chat manages reading and sending in meetings and events up to 1,000 attendees, including webinar organisers, presenters, co-organisers and attendees.
claims.quote: Whether participants in your users' meetings and events with up to 1,000 attendees can read and send chat messages.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance guidance; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not state whether the new separate webinar organiser and presenter chat follows the Meeting chat policy.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams webinar structured meeting private organizer presenter chat meeting chat policy default enabled. Read manage-meeting-chat, manage-event-chat and plan-events: general chat scope is stated, but the new separate chat is not described.

claims.claim: Town hall attendee chat is controlled at Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Events optimized for a large audience chat experience.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Events policies. Select the policy you want to edit or create a new one. In the Events optimized for a large audience chat experience dropdown list, select Optimized (the default value) or None.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TownhallChatExperience None prevents organisers from enabling attendee chat.
claims.quote: To turn off chat for attendees in events optimized for large audiences, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TownhallChatExperience None
claims.fix: Keep the call. Add to controls[2].note: "The Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy reference marks the events policy as preview." Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamseventspolicy?view=teams-ps.

claims.claim: The checklist asks for an eDiscovery content search, but the controls table has no eDiscovery search row.
claims.quote: Checklist: "Run an eDiscovery content search". Table: "Whether town hall organisers, co-organisers and presenters get backroom (event group) chat"; "Meeting chat policy"; "Whether town hall organisers can turn on attendee chat (not the event group chat)".
claims.fix: Remove the After rollout checklist bullet beginning "Run an eDiscovery content search"; it names a control absent from the table. Retain the existing eDiscovery test advice in Risk assessment rather than adding a control row.
